name: The St. Regis Resort Bora Bora
positioning: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort: overwater and beach villas on a motu reached by boat, with a private Lagoonarium and a spa on its own island
best_for: Couples who want a spacious overwater villa with glass floor panels
Snorkelers who want a protected lagoon sanctuary right at the resort

facts.text: The resort is on a motu, or islet, so boat transfers are needed to and from Bora Bora's airport and the main island.
The boat transfer from Bora Bora's airport to the resort takes 20 minutes.
The overwater villas have glass viewing panels cut into the floor, so you can watch tropical fish swim by.
Every overwater villa has a separate living room and bedroom.
The Royal Estate is a private compound enclosed on three sides by coral walls, opening onto its own private beach facing the lagoon and Mount Otemanu.
Snorkeling gear for the Lagoonarium is complimentary.
Guests can choose between the Main Pool with a swim-up bar and the Oasis Adults-Only Pool with private cabanas.
Te Pahu hosts a Polynesian show and dinner every Wednesday night.
Complimentary watersports at the Main Beach include stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking and local canoe.
A Cultural Ambassador leads activities such as flower crown making and pareo painting.
The resort was designed by Parisian architect Pierre Lacombe.
Every villa comes with a pair of beach cruiser-style bicycles.

highlights.text: The resort's overwater villas are the largest in French Polynesia and the South Pacific, starting at 1,550 square feet.
The resort's private Lagoonarium is a protected underwater sanctuary for tropical fish and coral, including Napoleon fish.
The spa sits on its own private island overlooking the Lagoonarium.
Lagoon Restaurant is suspended over the water, with views of Mount Otemanu, and showcases local produce and freshly caught seafood.
Breakfast can be delivered to your villa on a va'a, a traditional Polynesian canoe.

considerations.text: The complimentary shuttle to the main island and Vaitape runs once a day and not on Sundays or public holidays.
All spa bookings require a day pass.
WhataHotel notes that the remote French Polynesian location requires extensive travel time.
